title: BusemannFormer: Horospherical Self-Attention for Hyperbolic Graph Transformers
summary: BusemannFormer replaces standard dot-product self-attention in graph transformers with a hyperbolic attention kernel in which each query selects an ideal-boundary direction and scores keys by Busemann depth, plus an optional finite-boundary dictionary enabling linear-complexity global attention. Costs include implementation complexity of fully hyperbolic operations (no off-the-shelf serving stack or quantized kernels), potential numerical instability at the boundary, and unreported latency and memory overhead relative to standard attention. It can fail on non-hierarchical graphs where hyperbolic geometry offers no inductive bias, on datasets where the flat-limit behavior differs from tuned dot-product attention, and in maintenance since hyperbolic primitives are poorly supported by mainstream inference tooling.
rationale: The technique is only relevant if the reader runs graph transformers on strongly hierarchical data, and the abstract gives no quantified gain, cost profile, or production-ready evidence, so it warrants a small-scale experiment rather than adoption.
technique: Horospherical Busemann attention for hyperbolic graph transformers

BusemannFormer-LD reportedly outperforms evaluated baselines on several hierarchical and citation node-classification benchmarks; no multiplicative factor is stated in the abstract.
